title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts & API Examples — Docs Site Ops and Top Issues
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary

This document defines the standards, operating procedures, templates, and canonical fixes for developer-facing documentation produced by the Developer Experience (DevEx) team: SDK guides, quickstarts & templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the top support issues with canonical fixes. It is intended for DevEx authors, SDK owners, technical writers, and on-call support engineers.

Audience and scope

- Primary audience: Product engineers, SDK maintainers, solution engineers, support, and developer advocates.
- Scope: All public/internal SDK guides (Python, JavaScript, Go), quickstarts and templated starter projects, canonical API examples (REST + SDKs), docs-site workflows (authoring -> CI -> publish), and a prioritized list of top support issues with canonical fixes.

Goals

1. Provide consistent, runnable, and tested examples that reduce time-to-first-success for new users.
2. Reduce support volume by publishing canonical fixes for the top recurring issues.
3. Maintain an efficient authoring and publishing workflow with automated smoke tests and measurable SLAs for doc updates.

Document types and canonical locations

- SDK guides: confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site and quickstarts-and-templates. Each SDK guide must have a paired GitHub example repo.
- Quickstarts & templates: confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates. Templates include a README, sample app, and CI smoke test.
- API examples: confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/api-examples (examples must be provided as cURL + SDK snippet + runnable gist).
- Docs-site operating procedures: confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site.
- Top support issues & canonical fixes: confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates (this file).

Authoring standards (required metadata and structure)

Every page must include the following top-level metadata (document header):
- title (concise)
- summary (1-2 sentences)
- owner and secondary owner (team + individual)
- last_updated and reviewers
- labels (3-6 tags)

Recommended document structure:
1. Summary (1 para)
2. Who should read this
3. Prerequisites (API keys, account, SDK version)
4. Step-by-step quickstart (runnable)
5. Reference (API/CLI args, config table)
6. Troubleshooting / Common issues (links to canonical fixes)
7. Related pages and example repos
8. Change log / migration notes

Naming conventions and file names

- Use short, descriptive dashed filenames: e.g., "python-sdk-getting-started-2026.json".
- Quickstarts should include the year and optional version suffix (v1, v2) in the filename.

SDK guide requirements and checklist

Before publishing, the author must complete the checklist below. The docs CI will fail the PR if any required item is missing.

| Item | Required | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| README with steps | yes | copy-paste runnable commands
| Example app repo link | yes | link to org/example-repo
| CI smoke test | yes | run integration tests against staging API key
| Minimum SDK version | yes | state language and version (e.g., Python >= 1.4.0)
| Code snippets: cURL + SDK | yes | include both for parity
| Error handling example | yes | show retry/backoff pattern
| License & attribution | yes | include OSS license if applicable

Quickstarts & templates (recommended patterns)

We maintain the following quickstart templates: token-generation, chat-integration, embeddings-indexing, reranking-pipeline, streaming-output. Each template includes:
- brief overview and intended use-case
- prerequisites and estimated cost (GPU/compute estimates for local demos)
- step-by-step setup (CLI and UI steps)
- test commands and expected outputs

Template checklist (publish-ready):
- README with 5-minute setup
- package.json / pyproject.toml / go.mod for reproducible deps
- example test (unit or smoke) that runs in CI within 2 minutes
- LICENSE and CODE_OF_CONDUCT
- clear config file for API key (env var pattern: REDWOOD_API_KEY)

API examples: canonical patterns

All API examples must include three parallel variants: 1) cURL (raw REST), 2) Python SDK, 3) JavaScript SDK. Example canonical flows: text generation, streaming response, chat with function/tool calling, embeddings + vector search, and safety filters.

Example: Text generation (canonical cURL)

curl -X POST \
  https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.2", "input":"Write a short product description for a developer-first LLM inference platform." }'

Python SDK example (canonical)

from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"])
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-1.2", input="Write a short product description for a developer-first LLM inference platform.")
print(resp.text)

JS SDK example (canonical)

const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference')
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-1.2', input: 'Write a short product description for a developer-first LLM inference platform.' })
console.log(resp.text)

Docs-site operating procedures (authoring -> publish pipeline)

1. Authoring
   - Create branch: docs/<area>/<short-title>
   - Add page with required metadata and fill the template.
2. Review & approvals
   - Assign two reviewers (one SDK owner + one technical writer).
   - Use the "docs-review" label to trigger reviewer notification.
3. CI checks (run on PR)
   - Linter (confluence markdown style rules)
   - Link-checker (no 404s)
   - Code-snippet smoke tests (run examples against a staging API key stored in CI secrets)
   - Accessibility checks (alt text on all images)
4. Merge and publish\   - Merge to main and let docs pipeline publish to staging site.
   - On successful staging smoke tests, a release job will publish to the production docs site.

Rollback & emergency change process

- If a published doc contains serious errors (incorrect code that leaks secrets, or broken migration notes), open an emergency PR with label "docs-hotfix" and cc the on-call DevEx engineer. The docs pipeline supports immediate hotfix publishes.

Publishing SLAs and KPIs

- Minor updates (typo/clarity): target publish time <= 48 hours after merge.
- Major updates (API changes, new example flows): target publish time <= 5 business days (includes reviewer sign-off and CI).
- Docs QA: >= 95% of quickstarts must pass CI smoke tests on publish.

Top support issues and canonical fixes (2024-2026)

1) Issue: SDK example fails with HTTP 401 in CI and for new users
   - Symptom: cURL and SDK samples return 401 or "invalid API key".
   - Root cause: Example repos reference REDWOOD_API_KEY in a .env.sample but authors forget to include instructions to copy and set env. Some CI pipelines were not reading the correct secrets.
   - Canonical fix: 
     - Update quickstart README to include exact env var steps: `cp .env.sample .env && export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...`
     - Add a pre-merge CI check to verify that examples use environment variables (no inline API keys) and that smoke tests use the CI secret REDWOOD_DOCS_STAGING_KEY.
     - Owner: DevEx (Maya Chen) + SDK owners.

2) Issue: Streaming examples hang or cut off after ~4-8 seconds
   - Symptom: Users report truncated streaming outputs in browser-based quickstarts.
   - Root cause: Example frontends were using an incorrect fetch configuration (not reading server-sent events properly) and our WebSocket fallback was not enabled in the sample server.
   - Canonical fix:
     - Publish corrected client code (uses EventSource for SSE or WebSocket with ping/pong).
     - Add streaming smoke test that asserts partial response arrives within 500ms and final token within 3s for a short prompt.
     - Owner: SDK Web team (Jordan Lee).

3) Issue: Embeddings examples produce poor nearest-neighbor matches after model upgrade
   - Symptom: Search results degrade after switching embeddings model in quickstart examples.
   - Root cause: Upstream default model changed (v1.0 -> v1.1) with different embedding dimensionality; authors did not update vector index config or document re-ingestion instructions.
   - Canonical fix:
     - Add explicit model pinning in examples (e.g., "use redwood-embed-1.0 for this quickstart") and include migration steps to re-index data when changing embedding model dimensionality.
     - Provide a small migration script in the example repos.
     - Owner: Applied ML (Sofia Martinez) + DevEx.

4) Issue: Function/tool-calling examples produce malformed JSON when users copy/paste
   - Symptom: Function outputs fail to parse in user code.
   - Root cause: Examples used pretty-printed JSON in code comments without escaping in string literals, leading to syntax errors when pasted into languages with different string quoting rules.
   - Canonical fix:
     - Publish language-specific examples that construct payloads programmatically (not by copy-pasting raw JSON), and add unit-test examples that assert JSON serializes correctly.
     - Owner: SDK owners.

5) Issue: Docs broken links to example repos after repository reorganization
   - Symptom: 404s in docs link checker for example repos.
   - Root cause: Reorg in GitHub moved example repos to a new org path but docs were not updated.
   - Canonical fix:
     - Enforce link-checker on PRs and include a required step in the authoring checklist to verify example repo path.
     - Implement a lightweight redirect page strategy in the docs site to surface moved repos and capture telemetry.
     - Owner: DevEx + Platform.

Operational runbook snippets (for on-call)

- Problem: Docs smoke tests failing for an unrelated test after an SDK release
  1. Check CI logs and the redwood-docs-staging-key usage.
  2. If failure is due to SDK version mismatch, create rollback branch in example repo and pin SDK to previous known-good version.
  3. Notify SDK owners and create a postmortem doc if failure impacts > 10% of quickstarts.

Maintenance cadence and responsibilities

- Quarterly review: Each quickstart and SDK guide must be reviewed and validated quarterly by the owner.
- Release-aligned updates: When an SDK or API minor/major version is released, owners must update affected docs within 10 business days.
- Ownership matrix: Owners must be declared on each doc page (primary and secondary owner).

Metrics to track

- Docs CI pass rate (target >= 98%)
- Quickstart successful-run rate in CI (target >= 95%)
- Mean time to publish minor update (target <= 48 hours)
- Number of support tickets referencing docs (target: reduce by 30% year-over-year)

Appendix: helpful snippets and links

- ENV pattern: use REDWOOD_API_KEY for examples and REDWOOD_DOCS_STAGING_KEY for CI smoke tests.
- Example staging curl: `REDWOOD_API_KEY=$REDWOOD_DOCS_STAGING_KEY curl -s -X POST https://staging.api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"model\":\"redwood-1.2\",\"input\":\"hello\"}"`
- Example repos: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples (single source of truth for quickstarts)
- Docs style guide: confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/docs-style-guide-2025

If you are publishing a new quickstart and want help, ping #devex-docs on Slack or assign the DevEx on-call.

Change log

- 2025-11-14: Initial draft (Maya Chen).
- 2026-01-12: Added streaming tests and canonical fixes for streaming (Jordan Lee).
- 2026-02-28: Updated publishing SLA and CI smoke-test requirements (Sofia Martinez).
